claim: Leave rounds 1–3 with at least one RB. 2026 expert consensus is Hero RB, not rigid Zero RB — workhorse backs are scarce.
WR-first is a floor build in 10-team PPR; an elite RB in the first three is the ceiling build.
Wait on QB, K, and D/ST in a 10-team PPR. Streaming and late-round talent are deep enough that early spend is a tax.
O-line consensus: Denver, Philadelphia, Tampa Bay, and Buffalo are the top units; Cleveland, Miami, Tennessee, and Houston sit at the bottom.
Industry sleeper vs ADP: Packers RB with a path to early work if the committee breaks. Ranked well ahead of his ADP on expert boards.
Industry sleeper vs ADP: Broncos rookie RB behind a top O-line. Late-round stash if the workload opens.
Industry sleeper vs ADP: Jaguars WR who keeps showing up on value lists when the room is slower than experts.
Industry sleeper vs ADP: Panthers RB coming back from injury. Experts still rank him as a mid-round value if the role is there.
Industry sleeper vs ADP: Colts slot WR. PPR volume is the pitch; ADP often lags expert ranks.
Industry sleeper vs ADP: Packers WR whose expert rank is typically ahead of ESPN ADP.
Industry sleeper vs ADP: Packers TE with every-week usage. Often cheaper in this room than on expert boards.
